  CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  APRIL 9, 2024

  A regular and special meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor Brock at 5:36
  p.m., on Tuesday, April 9, 2024, at City Council Chambers, 1685 Main Street, Santa Monica, CA.

  Roll Call:  Present:  Mayor Phil Brock
  Mayor Pro Tem Lana Negrete (arrived at 5:39 p.m.)
  Councilmember Gleam Davis
  Councilmember Oscar de la Torre
  Councilmember Christine Parra
  Councilmember Caroline Torosis (arrived at 5:43 p.m.)

  City Attorney Douglas Sloan
  Interim City Clerk Nikima S. Newsome

  members present except Councilmember Torosis and Mayor Pro Tem
  Negrete. Councilmember Parra led the assemblage in the Pledge of
  Allegiance.

  LEVINE ACT  Pursuant to the Levine Act (Govt Code Section 84308), any party to a
  DISCLOSURE  permit, license, contract, or other entitlement before the Council is
  required to disclose on the record any contribution, including
  (Mayor Pro Tem Negrete  aggregated contributions, of more than $250 made by the party or the
  arrived at 5:39 p.m.)  party's agents within the preceding 12 months to any City official.
  Participants and agents are requested to make this disclosure as well.
  The disclosure must include the name of the party, participant, or agent,
  and any other person making the contribution; the name of the
  recipient, the amount of the contribution, and the date the contribution
  was made.

  STAFF  11.A. Business License Tax Modernization, was presented.
  ADMINISTRATIVE
  ITEMS:  Recommended Action
  BUSINESS LICENSE TAX  Staff recommends that City Council:
  MODERNIZATION  1. Consider the proposed Business License Modernization and
  associated business license tax rate changes;
  2. Direct staff to draft changes, as applicable to section of Article 6
  Business, Professions and Trades;
  3. Prepare a draft measure for the Business License Modernization and
  a proposed resolution to place the measure on the November 2024
  ballot: and
  4. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to
  Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines.

  Questions asked and answered of staff included what was the purpose of the
  $75.00 fee; is there anything being done to incentivize workers to return to
  the office in the City; what is the history of the tax cap; would the proposed
  staggered rate be counter-productive to bringing more employers back into
  the office; will the tax rate be fixed or will it increase over time and can the
  definitions of businesses be expanded.

  AFFORDABLE HOUSING  11.B. Approval of Design Concept for Affordable Housing
  Development located on City-owned Site located at 1318 Fourth Street
  and Negotiate Ground Lease and Disposition and Development
  Agreement, was presented.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Select Design Concept #1 for the affordable housing development
  located at 1318 Fourth Street, Santa Monica, CA 90401 (PS3) – 122
  apartments with 2 levels of underground parking;
  2. Direct staff to proceed with negotiations of the Ground Lease and
  Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) with developer
  EAH, Inc.; and
  3. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect on the
  environment for providing direction on development concept
  pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines and find
  that the future development of affordable housing on the City-owned
  properties at 1318 Fourth Street is consistent with the certified 6th
  Cycle Housing Element Environmental Impact Report (State
  Clearinghouse No. 2020100575).

  Questions asked and answered of staff included are union workers not being
  employed for this project; has there been discussions as to what type of
  grocery store will being going into this space; what elements will be part of
  the design as it pertains to the availability of natural light and nature; how
  many parking spaces; what is the vision for the grocery space as far as
  parking; will the entire first floor be a grocery store and what is the proposed
  square footage; will the grocery store hire locally; how does the size of the
  grocery store compare to others; will the work/live concept be prioritized so
  that those who work in the City will receive priority with obtaining housing;
  is there anyway to build this project more quickly; is there any possibility of
  lowering the per unit cost and will any concessions need to be made to
  increase the building by one floor.

  Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to
  community serving space; holding subcontractors accountable to pay
  prevailing wage and concerns with the amount of proposed parking spaces.

  Motion by Councilmember Torosis, seconded by Councilmember Davis, to
  adopt the staff recommendation.

  ESTABLISHMENT  Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk develop and return to City
  Council with recommendations to establish a Youth Commission (or
  Council) based on best practices. The City currently engages youth at
  PAL (Youth Leadership Council), Virginia Avenue Park (Teen
  Leadership Council), and the Library (Teen Leadership Council) and a
